title: Move stock between bins without losing a unit

blocks.text: The warehouse keeps its stock in one `ConcurrentHashMap`: for each SKU, how many units sit in each bin. Pickers move units between bins all day. The same map is read by the hourly stock count and updated by the order service, which ships units straight from it with its own `compute` calls. Lately the stock count has reported units missing that turned up an hour later, a bin once showed -6 units, and a shipment of glue reappeared on the shelf in the system but not in the aisle.

Finish `move(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Warehouse.java`. The `Bins` record and the reading methods are done. The order service won't change, so whatever `move` does must hold against its calls on the map. When you're done, a stock count taken at any moment finds every unit, no bin goes below zero, and no shipment is undone. About seven lines in total.
The tests hold the picker's thread right after it reads the map, or right after it first changes it, and meanwhile take a stock count or ship from the same bin.

cases.says: a move shifts units from one bin to another, and a move that asks for more than the bin holds, or for an unknown SKU, changes nothing
a stock count taken while a move is in progress finds every unit of the SKU
units shipped while a move is deciding are not moved as well, so no bin goes negative
a move that runs alongside a shipment never puts the shipped units back

origin.section: compute and merge Are Atomic for One Key, Not for an Action Across Keys

concepts: ConcurrentHashMap.compute and merge are atomic for one call on one key; an action made of two calls can be seen half done, so values that must agree go under one key.
